column.text: Bitcoin is holding its $80,000 line after a weekend that punished leverage. A flush erased $838M in crypto positions over 24 hours, mostly longs, and $404M of long liquidations landed in four hours as BTC slipped briefly below $80,000. The session closed with a broad rally, BTC back above $80,000 and ETH up 1.8%. Flows tell a split story. Bitcoin ETFs took $137.9M out on Friday, 23 Oct, yet are up $223.9M over seven days. Ether's Friday inflow was $4.4M against a seven-day net of negative $350.7M, and Solana's seven-day net is negative $40.1M. Macro money remains cautious. The micro picture is firmer: one whale holding a 93,184 ETH long worth $214M injected $5.67M of USDC to stay alive, lowering its liquidation price to roughly $2,177 to $2,181 while sitting on $18.62M in unrealized losses. Our regime reads RISK_OFF, but a falling tape is not a short signal. Shorts need a mechanism visible in the printed data, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need real proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20-day MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. Dip-buying is not a plan. Fear & Greed sits at 54 and dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure decides this one. Watch Basel crypto exposure rules and the digital euro, which an ECB official says could launch as early as 2029. Hold $80,000 on a daily close and the squeeze has room to run; lose it and the flush becomes the trend.
